The arguments and their roles are distinct. `BIRT` uses parameters like `?n` and `?p` representing entities and items, while `PUSS` uses `?jack` and `?puss` representing the cat and its owner. The preconditions and effects also differ in their specific details, reflecting the different contexts of the actions.  The types are the same, but the specific actions and their associated parameters demonstrate a different semantic interpretation of ‘has’.
